- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if price is trending down.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast increase to 2–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of forecast > true outcome, apply downward correction by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion — use 3-day moving average of true prices as baseline for next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) — apply 1–2% downward bias to first 5 forecasts if sentiment is weak or mixed.  
- If true price drops sharply after a forecast spike, model often fails to adjust — add 1–2% downward correction if true price drops > 2% from forecast peak.
